title: The Widow's Offering and the Destruction of Jerusalem

questions.question: Looking up, Jesus saw the rich putting their gifts into the offering box. Who did He see putting in two small copper coins?
options: A poor widow
A blind beggar
A leper outside the walls
A crippled tax collector
questions.explanation: Luke 21:2 (ESV): "and he saw a poor widow put in two small copper coins."

questions.question: Why did Jesus say that the poor widow put in more than all of them?
options: "For they all contributed out of their abundance, but she out of her poverty put in all she had to live on."
"Because the copper was blessed by the high priest prior."
"Because her prayer was genuine while theirs were false murmurs."
"Because the Lord values the smallest tokens above gold."
questions.correctAnswer: "For they all contributed out of their abundance, but she out of her poverty put in all she had to live on."
questions.explanation: Luke 21:4 (ESV): "For they all contributed out of their abundance, but she out of her poverty put in all she had to live on."

questions.question: When some spoke of the temple, how it was adorned with noble stones and offerings, what did Jesus prophesy?
options: "As for these things that you see, the days will come when there will not be left here one stone upon another that will not be thrown down."
"The gold will be stripped and given to Caesar."
"This temple will be restored entirely to the glory of Solomon's era."
"A great earthquake will swallow it into the earth forever."
questions.correctAnswer: "As for these things that you see, the days will come when there will not be left here one stone upon another that will not be thrown down."
questions.explanation: Luke 21:6 (ESV): "As for these things that you see, the days will come when there will not be left here one stone upon another that will not be thrown down."

questions.question: Jesus warned His disciples that many will come in His name saying, "I am he!" and "The time is at hand!" What did He command regarding them?
options: "Do not go after them."
"Rebuke them fiercely in the synagogues."
"Ask them to turn water into wine as a test."
"Bring them to the ruling elders."
questions.explanation: Luke 21:8 (ESV): "And he said, 'See that you are not led astray. For many will come in my name, saying, "I am he!" and, "The time is at hand!" Do not go after them.'"

questions.question: When they hear of wars and tumults, what does Jesus say must happen first, though the end will not be at once?
options: Do not be terrified, for these things must first take place
Hide yourselves in the mountains immediately
Flee across the sea to distant islands
Stockpile your wheat and fast for forty days
questions.correctAnswer: Do not be terrified, for these things must first take place
questions.explanation: Luke 21:9 (ESV): "And when you hear of wars and tumults, do not be terrified, for these things must first take place, but the end will not be at once."

questions.question: Jesus said that before the great signs from heaven happen, they will lay hands on the disciples and persecute them, delivering them to kings and governors. What did He say this will be an opportunity for?
options: To bear witness
To show their mighty strength in battle
To escape by invisible means entirely
To overthrow the government in truth
questions.explanation: Luke 21:13 (ESV): "This will be your opportunity to bear witness."

questions.question: Jesus told the disciples not to meditate beforehand how to answer their persecutors. Why?
options: "For I will give you a mouth and wisdom, which none of your adversaries will be able to withstand or contradict."
"Because the angels will cast a spell of confusion upon the courts."
"Because silence is the strongest armor against lies."
"Your lawyers will speak boldly on your behalf."
questions.correctAnswer: "For I will give you a mouth and wisdom, which none of your adversaries will be able to withstand or contradict."
questions.explanation: Luke 21:15 (ESV): "for I will give you a mouth and wisdom, which none of your adversaries will be able to withstand or contradict."

questions.question: Jesus warned that disciples will be delivered up even by parents, brothers, relatives, and friends. By whom will they be hated?
options: "And you will be hated by all for my name's sake."
"By the Romans alone."
"By the Gentile nations utterly."
"By the wealthy elite securely."
questions.correctAnswer: "And you will be hated by all for my name's sake."
questions.explanation: Luke 21:17 (ESV): "You will be hated by all for my name's sake."

questions.question: "But not a hair of your head will perish. By your..." what, "...you will gain your lives"?
options: endurance
sword
cleverness
fasting
questions.explanation: Luke 21:19 (ESV): "By your endurance you will gain your lives."

questions.question: When you see Jerusalem surrounded by armies, what should you know has come near?
options: Its desolation
Its ultimate victory entirely
The millennium of peace
The return of Elijah
questions.explanation: Luke 21:20 (ESV): "But when you see Jerusalem surrounded by armies, then know that its desolation has come near."

questions.question: Who should flee to the mountains when Jerusalem's desolation nears?
options: Those who are in Judea
Those hidden in the temple courts safely
The merchants selling goods in the streets
The Roman governors ruling the province
questions.explanation: Luke 21:21 (ESV): "Then let those who are in Judea flee to the mountains, and let those who are inside the city depart, and let not those who are out in the country enter it,"

questions.question: Jesus describes signs in sun, moon, and stars, and people fainting with fear. Then they will see the Son of Man coming in a cloud with power and great glory. When these things begin to take place, what should the disciples do?
options: Straighten up and raise your heads, because your redemption is drawing near
Fall on your faces shivering in complete dread
Lock the doors of your houses until it passes entirely
Gnash your teeth mourning the destruction bitterly
questions.correctAnswer: Straighten up and raise your heads, because your redemption is drawing near
questions.explanation: Luke 21:28 (ESV): "Now when these things begin to take place, straighten up and raise your heads, because your redemption is drawing near."

questions.question: Jesus told a parable saying to look at the fig tree. What happens when its leaves come out?
options: You see for yourselves and know that the summer is already near
You know the harvest is ruined completely by frost
You prepare to chop it down entirely
The soil must be watered heavily for seven days
questions.correctAnswer: You see for yourselves and know that the summer is already near
questions.explanation: Luke 21:30 (ESV): "As soon as they come out in leaf, you see for yourselves and know that the summer is already near."

questions.question: Jesus assures that "Heaven and earth will pass away, but..."?
options: "...my words will not pass away."
"...the angels will rebuild it anew."
"...those written in the book persist forever."
"...the holy mountain stands unmoved."
questions.explanation: Luke 21:33 (ESV): "Heaven and earth will pass away, but my words will not pass away."

questions.question: Jesus warned them to watch themselves lest their hearts be weighed down with dissipation, drunkenness, and cares of this life. They are commanded to do what at all times?
options: Stay awake at all times, praying that you may have strength to escape all these things that are going to take place
Offer animal sacrifices daily to ensure their safety
Sing psalms loudly from the rooftops to ward off evil
Fast completely every second day until he returns
questions.correctAnswer: Stay awake at all times, praying that you may have strength to escape all these things that are going to take place
questions.explanation: Luke 21:36 (ESV): "But stay awake at all times, praying that you may have strength to escape all these things that are going to take place, and to stand before the Son of Man."

key_verse_text: "Heaven and earth will pass away, but my words will not pass away."
